full_judgment: 3. Thereafter, Benode Behari Paul died, leaving behind two sons Radha Ballav Paul and Hari Das Paul, and a widow, Shyam Prioshi Dasya as his heirs and successors. They were in possession of one-third share. Ram Lal Paul sold his one-third share by a registered sale deed to Bhim Chand and Janaki Nath Basak. Bhim Chand and Janaki Nath Basak sold their one-third share to Renuka Paul, wife of Ram Lal Paul, by a registered sale deed. Nitya Lal Paul was the owner of one-third share from his father Jadunath Paul. Thereafter, Nitya Lal Paul for himself and as constituted attorney on behalf of Shyam Prioshi Paul, and Radha Ballam Paul, Ram Lal Paul on behalf of Renuka Paul and Hari Das Paul executed a deed of sale on 29.3.1950 in favour of Musammat Anowari Begum. Anowari Begum got her name recorded during S.A. Operation in the S.A. Khatian No. 1591 and paid rent to the government and taxes to the Dhaka Municipal Corporation in her name. She executed and registered a general power of attorney in favour of her son, Harun-ur-Rashid on 21.9.1968. Thereafter, the said attorney, Harun-ur-Rashid, on behalf of Anowari Begum transferred the holding concerned in favour of Md. Ansar All petitioner No. 2 and Rejaul Huq, predecessor of petitioner No. by two registered sale deeds. During R.S. operation, their names were recorded in R.S. Khatian and they paid rents and taxes to the authorities concerned. Thereafter Rezaul Huq died, leaving behind his three sons, namely, Mozammel Huq, Mofazzel Huq and Serajul Hug, Mozammel Huq and Serajul Huq transferred their share in favour of petitioner No. 1 who got possession of the same and had been possessing the same along with petitioner No. 2, in 1982, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka respondent No. 2 made a proposal to declare the property as Enemy Property or Vested Property. The petitioners raised serious objection. The petitioners recorded their names in the mutation Khatian in the office of Assistant Commissioner (Land) Kotwali, Dhaka-vide Mutation case No. 239(S) P-II/74-75 dated 12.9.74 of C.O. (Revenue) Kotwali Circle, and paid rent to the government. When the petitioners went to pay the ground rents to the concerned Tahshil office, the Tahshilder (Satrapur Tahshil) informed the petitioners on 20.9.95 that the property concerned had been declared as abandoned and no rent would be received from the petitioners.
